request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (50,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 37.2% (95% band 34.8% to 39.5%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.272: -0.65; 0.272 <= x < 0.461: -0.3; 0.461 <= x < 0.606: +0.1; 0.606 <= x < 0.648: +0.66; 0.648 <= x < 0.688: +1.12; 0.688 <= x < 0.738: +1.8; 0.738 <= x < 0.802: +2.5; x >= 0.802: +3.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.07, 95% band [+2.91, +3.31]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 23.2% (95% band 20.0% to 23.7%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.2; >= 2: +0.62 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.99, 95% band [+0.88, +1.03]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 11.9% (95% band 10.2% to 12.6%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 33,100: +0.36; 33,100 <= x < 69,100: +0.033; x >= 69,100: -0.27 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.81, 95% band [-0.93, -0.66]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 10.0% (95% band 8.3% to 11.1%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 97.3: +0.3; 97.3 <= x < 212: -0.012; x >= 212: -0.17 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.66, 95% band [-0.73, -0.52]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 7.9% (95% band 6.7% to 9.2%); rank 4 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.432: -0.07; x >= 0.432: +0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.36, 95% band [+0.28, +0.47]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 3.8% (95% band 2.5% to 5.3%); rank 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2: -0.02; >= 3: +0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.22, 95% band [+0.14, +0.34]).
- `feature_b`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.4% to 2.6%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.03, 95% band [-0.06, +0.11]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.3% to 2.4%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.05, 95% band [-0.15, +0.03]).
- `feature_a`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.3% to 2.2%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.03, 95% band [-0.02, +0.11]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `history_months & age`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.60 (95% band -0.72 to -0.46) when `age` = 23.7, -0.81 (95% band -0.96 to -0.53) when `age` = 72.3.
  Effect of `age` from 23.7 to 72.3: +0.05 (95% band -0.14 to +0.14) when `history_months` = 24.2, -0.16 (95% band -0.32 to +0.02) when `history_months` = 343.
- `history_months & feature_b`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.70 (95% band -0.76 to -0.52) when `feature_b` = -1.66, -0.57 (95% band -0.72 to -0.43) when `feature_b` = 1.65.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.66 to 1.65: -0.03 (95% band -0.09 to +0.11) when `history_months` = 24.2, +0.11 (95% band -0.06 to +0.19) when `history_months` = 343.
- `income & feature_b`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 1.5%).
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 114,000: -0.93 (95% band -1.06 to -0.67) when `feature_b` = -1.66, -0.75 (95% band -0.89 to -0.59) when `feature_b` = 1.65.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.66 to 1.65: -0.06 (95% band -0.17 to +0.11) when `income` = 22,000, +0.12 (95% band -0.06 to +0.23) when `income` = 114,000.
- 2 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 0.7%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by revolving credit utilization, which accounts for about 37% of its importance and has the largest effect: applicants using a high share of their credit limit are much more likely to default, with the risk rising by about 3 units on the log-odds scale between the 5th and 95th percentile of utilization."},{"id":2,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver (about 23%): applicants with no past delinquencies carry lower predicted risk, one delinquency adds a little, and two or more add a clearer increase in risk."},{"id":3,"text":"Income and length of credit history matter less (about 12% and 10% of importance), with higher income and longer credit histories both associated with lower predicted default risk, and the effect of income is strongest at the lower end of its range."},{"id":4,"text":"The debt-to-income ratio contributes a modest increase in risk above roughly 0.43, and recent credit inquiries contribute a small increase at three or more, at about 8% and 4% of importance respectively."},{"id":5,"text":"Age, feature_a and feature_b have very little influence: their effects are small and their uncertainty bands include zero, so the data do not establish that they affect predictions."},{"id":6,"text":"The interactions are modest: the effect of credit history length is somewhat weaker for applicants with higher feature_b values and for older applicants, and the effect of income is stronger for applicants with lower feature_b values, but these interactions together account for only about 2% of importance and some of their uncertainty bands cross zero."},{"id":7,"text":"Overall, the model's predictions rest mostly on how heavily an applicant uses existing credit and on their record of delinquencies, with income and credit history as secondary factors."}]}
